title: Paryantapañcāśikā — Fifty Verses of the Uttermost
author: Abhinavagupta
text:
The Paryantapañcāśikā is a work of fifty verses in eight portions, ascribed to Abhinavagupta and preserved in his collected works. Its object is what the tradition holds uttermost: speech filled with rest, the unspeakable studied as the very heart of things. The verses trace how what cannot be said is not thereby lost — how knowings, sundered and varied as they shine, still converge on a single ground that no statement captures and no statement has ever missed.

Its juice: the fifty verses are a sustained exercise in speaking the unspeakable without embarrassment. Their gift is to show that the limit of language is not a wall but the shape of what language keeps circling — and that the circling, done precisely, is itself a form of knowledge.
